about: The roadmap of the port. To pick the next step: the first planned step with no owner whose earlier steps in the same phase it needs are done. Claim a step by writing your thread's title as its `owner` (and status `started`), in a small pull request merged before you start, so nothing is done twice. `done_when` is the test a step must pass. The pull request that ships a step sets `status` to done, `post` to the slug of its devlog post and `pr` to its number. Steps may be added, split or dropped; the post of the step that caused it says why.

milestones.title: First light
milestones.proof: nimaki draws every pie and timeline of the corpus byte for byte as Pele 1.13.0 does in Node, with the same text measurer.

milestones.title: diagrammari without Node
milestones.proof: Flowchart and sequence identical to Pele on their corpus and on the examples of diagrammari; a proposal for diagrammari to use nimaki for these types.

milestones.title: Every diagram type
milestones.proof: Every row of the coverage map is done or a recorded divergence: all 34 corpus files and the compat inputs identical.

milestones.title: Everywhere
milestones.proof: The same renderer compiled with nim js draws in the browser on the pages; a C ABI build for other languages; a routine to follow new Pele releases.

phases.title: Before the first line
phases.goal: A place for the port to happen, the tools to check it, and the context to understand it: what Pele and Mermaid are, how diagrams are drawn from text, and the plan.

steps.title: The stage: conventions, roadmap, coverage map, CI
steps.what: AGENTS.md adapted from gleam-in-nim, the pin of Pele in reference/PIN and on every page, the roadmap with owners, the coverage map (diagram types × parse, layout, render), decision records, setup script, Pages CI, the nimib skeleton and its first post.
steps.done_when: The site builds in CI and deploys from main; links and drift checks pass.
steps.owner: Set up nimaki foundation and tooling

steps.title: The referee: difftest against Pele in Node
steps.what: tools/corpus.mjs builds corpus/cases.json (2,118 cases of 33 types from Pele's corpus and compat specs); tools/oracle.mjs runs the pinned npm package in Node; tools/difftest.nim renders each case with nimaki and compares byte for byte, per type, showing the first differing byte, with a self test and --check-done in CI.
steps.done_when: difftest runs in CI, reports every case as unsupported today, and its self test shows it catches a one-byte difference.
steps.owner: Set up nimaki foundation and tooling

steps.title: A look of its own
steps.what: Design nimaki's theme for the pages (docs/theme.nim, fonts in docs/assets/) to replace the placeholder borrowed from gleam-in-nim, in two modes, phone first.
steps.done_when: Every page builds with the new look in both modes; a phone-width preview is reviewed.

steps.title: Pele, where it comes from
steps.what: Why kepano built Pele (size, speed, theming, the security of diagrams in Obsidian), how it was announced, how fast it moved (22 npm releases in 25 days), how it is tested, its contribution and AI policy. Every claim linked.
steps.owner: Research Pele, Mermaid and diagram uses

steps.title: What Mermaid is
steps.what: History and people, the diagram types and how they arrived, the grammars (Jison, Langium), how mermaid.js renders (dagre, ELK, a browser to measure text) and why so many headless reimplementations exist.
steps.owner: Research Pele, Mermaid and diagram uses

steps.title: The family of diagram tools
steps.what: Other Mermaid renderers and ports (beautiful-mermaid, merman, ariel-rs, mermaid-rs-renderer, mmdflux, selkie, Mermaider, Naiad) and the tools before and beside it (Graphviz, PlantUML, D2, Pikchr, ELK, dagre): what each gets right, and which ideas or corpora the port can reuse, with their licences.
steps.owner: Research Pele, Mermaid and diagram uses

steps.title: What diagrams are for
steps.what: Notable uses of Mermaid-style diagrams: documentation, GitHub and GitLab, Obsidian and notes, architecture, teaching, AI assistants that answer in diagrams. Which types people draw most, so the order of the port can follow.
steps.owner: Research Pele, Mermaid and diagram uses

steps.title: Drawing diagrams from text, from scratch
steps.what: Parsing one grammar per type, layered (Sugiyama) layout explained simply, Pele's own layered, compound and lane layouts, measuring text without a browser, writing SVG. For a reader who has never written a parser or a layout engine.
steps.done_when: A devlog post (or a short series) with a toy that runs on the page.
steps.owner: Explain diagram rendering and Pele architecture

steps.title: How Pele is built
steps.what: src/diagrams/<type>/ (parser, model, layout, renderer) and the shared layout/, text/, svg/: what each does, how big each is, where its decisions come from.
steps.done_when: A devlog post whose numbers come from the coverage map data.
steps.owner: Explain diagram rendering and Pele architecture

steps.title: What other AI-driven ports teach us
steps.what: What gleam-in-nim found (its devlog, decisions, AGENTS.md) and what is new for a port from TypeScript: UTF-16, JavaScript numbers, regexes, structural types.
steps.done_when: A devlog post; the porting guide gains its idiom map.

steps.title: The port plan
steps.what: Order of the parts and types, non-overlapping steps, and the verification: compat specs, render and layout snapshots, differential fuzzing against Pele in Node, real diagrams (diagrammari). Updated after every step.
steps.done_when: A devlog post and this roadmap revised.

phases.title: The core, and pie
phases.goal: The whole chain under a diagram, end to end, on the smallest type: measure text, write SVG, theme it, render pie byte for byte.

steps.title: JavaScript numbers and strings in Nim
steps.what: The number formatter (num() and JavaScript's number-to-string) and UTF-16 string helpers, tested against Node.
steps.done_when: Identical to Node on a large sample of numbers and strings.

steps.title: Measuring text: src/text
steps.what: The metrics measurer and its font tables, labels, entities. Checked through pie's labels (corpus and fuzzer); the label features other types use (Markdown, icons, math, wrapping) are ported and are checked as those types arrive.
steps.done_when: Widths identical to Pele's metricsMeasurer on every label of the corpus.

steps.title: Writing SVG: src/svg
steps.what: The builder, palette, theme, root, title.

steps.title: Detect, preprocess, render
steps.what: detect.ts, preprocess.ts, errors.ts, core.ts render(), the registry, the YAML front matter reader.
steps.done_when: Type detection and errors identical to Pele on every corpus input.

steps.title: Pie
steps.what: src/diagrams/pie: parser, model, render.

steps.title: Timeline
steps.what: src/diagrams/timeline, with common/scan.ts, common/fit.ts and the arrow marker of svg/edges.ts.
steps.owner: Port Pele core, pie and timeline

phases.title: Layered layout, flowchart and sequence
phases.goal: The layout most types stand on, and the two types people draw most.

steps.title: The layered layout: src/layout
steps.what: layered.ts and compound.ts, explained as they are ported; lanes.ts and components.ts come with swimlane and class.
steps.done_when: Exercised through flowchart; Pele's layout invariants replayed.

steps.title: Flowchart
steps.what: src/diagrams/flowchart, with the shared shapes and edges.

steps.title: Sequence
steps.what: src/diagrams/sequence.

steps.title: diagrammari's examples as a corpus
steps.what: Collect the Mermaid text that diagrammari's builders and spec examples write, and add it to corpus/ as a second source of cases.
steps.done_when: difftest runs on them; the cases are counted on the coverage map.

steps.title: Differential fuzzing
steps.what: Mutated inputs (seeded, as Pele's own mutator does) compared with the oracle, for the ported types.
steps.done_when: A seeded fuzz run in CI with --fast finds no differences on the ported types.

steps.title: A proposal for diagrammari
steps.what: How diagrammari could use nimaki instead of Node for the ported types, written as a proposal (diagrammari is not changed from here).
steps.done_when: A devlog post with the proposal.

steps.title: Check the label features against Pele
steps.what: Markdown, icons, math and line wrapping in labels (src/text) were ported with pie and left draft. Targeted corpus cases and a label fuzzer compare them with Pele across the types that use them; wanted differences go to the divergences page. Left for the next start: the second reading of src/text (decision 0005), which moves those files from draft to verified.
steps.done_when: A label fuzz run in CI finds no differences, and the text files move from draft to verified.
steps.owner: Verify labels and Pele's test suites

steps.title: Run Pele's own test suites
steps.what: Pele's tests at the pin (tests/compat, tests/render, tests/layout and the per-type tests) hold inputs and expectations beyond the difftest corpus. Their inputs go through the port and the oracle, and their checks are ported where they test the port's own functions.
steps.done_when: Every input of those suites gives the same result in nimaki as in Pele, or a divergence says why; the files they cover move from draft to verified.

phases.title: Everywhere
phases.goal: The port out of its repository: in the browser, in other languages, and following Pele.

steps.title: nimaki in the browser
steps.what: The same renderer compiled with nim js, checked by the referee (difftest --js) in Node and in CI.
steps.done_when: difftest passes on the JS build.

steps.title: nimaki drawing in the browser
steps.what: A browser entry point for the JavaScript build (render(text) exported), a page whose diagrams nimaki draws in the reader's browser, and a smaller file.
steps.done_when: a page draws its diagrams with nimaki in the browser, identical to the SVG drawn at build time.

steps.title: A C ABI
steps.what: A shared library for other languages (diagrammari-py).
steps.done_when: A Python smoke test renders a pie.

steps.title: Following Pele
steps.what: A routine that diffs a new Pele release against the pin and ports the changes.
steps.done_when: The pin moves once, with a post.

phases.title: Along the way
phases.goal: Steps that recur while the port goes on: articles that explain nimaki's own code (its overall structure, one module, or a pattern that comes back), because explaining code is a way to review it. What an article uncovers becomes a note for the thread that owns the code, or a new step here.

steps.title: The shape of the port
steps.what: A tour of nimaki's Nim code as it stands on main: how the files map to Pele's, the path of one diagram through render(), the shared parts every type leans on, and what the tour uncovered.
steps.done_when: A devlog post whose numbers come from the code on main; findings filed as notes or roadmap steps.

steps.title: Articles on the code, every once in a while
steps.what: A recurring step: every so often, one article on a module or a pattern of the port (the lexers, the layered layout, JavaScript's numbers and strings in Nim, the referee). Each article is its own step in this phase, claimed here first.
steps.done_when: Never: it recurs while the port goes on. Each article ships with its post and its findings.
